key_insight: The paper shows that common GNN explainer benchmarks can be misleading because the model may solve the task using spurious cues, so it compiles GNNs from logic to create models with known, exact explanations.
engineering_relevance: It provides a more rigorous testbed for graph explainability tools, helping engineers diagnose whether explainers are robust to indirect effects and equivalent model implementations.
method: Introduced Gracr, a compiler that translates graded modal logic formulas into GNN weights.
Built GracrBench from compiled GNNs so the ground-truth explanation is known by construction.
Evaluated 11 explainers across 6 tasks to probe fine-grained failure modes.
evidence_signal: Across six tasks and eleven explainers, the benchmark exposed that many explainers are not robust to indirect influences or alternative implementations of the same formula.
watch_item: The approach depends on compileable logic-based tasks, so its coverage may not fully represent explanation behavior on real-world GNNs trained from data.
paper_title: Beyond Trained Models: Compiling GNNs for a Sound Explainer Benchmark
